title: Choose a point on the curve

predict.q: The economy starts at 5% unemployment and 2% inflation. The government boosts AD and unemployment falls to 3%. What happens to inflation in the short run?

options.s: It stays at 2%, because inflation depends only on the money supply
options.fb: In the short run, a rise in AD that cuts unemployment also pushes up wages and prices.

options.s: It falls, because more people in work produce more goods
options.fb: More output, but higher demand for workers pushes up wages and prices: inflation rises.

options.s: It rises to about 4%: the economy moves up along the curve
options.fb: The point moves up along the SRPC: 3% unemployment, 4% inflation.

options.s: It rises, because the whole curve shifts up
options.fb: Moving AD moves the economy along the curve. The curve shifts only if something else changes.

task: Move the unemployment slider from 5% down to 3% and watch inflation.

target.do: Move the unemployment slider down to 3%, then press Check.

takeaway: On the short-run curve, lower unemployment costs higher inflation.
